snapshot.title: TNPSC REVISION: Economy Finale (Days 43–48)
snapshot.exam_hook: ⚡ TNPSC Economy Hook: Economy complete. Institutional dates. Welfare schemes. Tax amendments. Poverty committees. Victory. ⚡ v12 Stamina Hook: 60-min Sprint active.

quick_notes.title: Institutions Recap
quick_notes.detail: PC (1950). NITI (2015). FC (Art 280). GST (101st Amend). RBI (1935).
quick_notes.explanation: The Planning Commission (PC) was a government body created in 1950 to make five-year plans for India's economic development. It was replaced in 2015 by the NITI Aayog (NITI), which stands for National Institution for Transforming India, and now works with state governments on long-term policy goals. The Finance Commission (FC) is a constitutional body established under Article 280 of the Indian Constitution, which means it is appointed every five years to recommend how tax money should be shared between the central government and the states. The Goods and Services Tax (GST) was introduced by the 101st Amendment to the Constitution in 2016, which created a single national tax on goods and services to replace many separate state and central taxes. The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) was established in 1935 as the country's central bank, meaning it controls the printing of currency, manages the money supply, and regulates all other banks in India.

quick_notes.title: Planning Recap
quick_notes.explanation: The first Five-Year Plan, from 1951 to 1956, focused mainly on agriculture, which means growing crops and raising animals for food. The second Five-Year Plan, from 1956 to 1961, focused on industry, which means building factories and making things like machines and steel. There was a period called a "Plan Holiday" from 1966 to 1969, which means the government paused making new five-year plans because of problems like drought and war. In 1991, India started a big change called LPG, which stands for Liberalization (opening the economy to private companies), Privatization (selling government-owned businesses to private owners), and Globalization (connecting India's economy with the world).

quick_notes.title: Poverty Recap
quick_notes.explanation: The Tendulkar Committee in 2009 set the official method for measuring poverty in India by calculating the minimum income needed to buy enough food and basic necessities. The Lorenz Curve is a graph that shows how income or wealth is spread across a population, helping to see inequality, which means the gap between the rich and the poor. The Gini Coefficient, or Gini index, is a number from 0 to 1 that measures this inequality, where 0 means everyone has the same income and 1 means one person has all the income. Disguised unemployment is a situation in agriculture where more people are working on a farm than are actually needed, so removing some workers does not reduce the total output.

quick_notes.title: Schemes Recap
quick_notes.explanation: MGNREGA stands for the Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act, passed in 2005. This law guarantees every adult in a rural household up to 100 days of paid work per year doing unskilled manual labor, like digging canals or building roads, and if the government fails to provide work within 15 days, it must pay an unemployment allowance. NABARD stands for the National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development, established in 1982, and it is a government-owned bank that provides loans and financial support to farmers, small businesses, and rural development projects across India. Mahalir Thittam, launched in 1989, is a Tamil Nadu government scheme that forms and supports women's self-help groups, giving them training and small loans to start their own businesses and become financially independent. Ujjwala, officially called the Pradhan Mantri Ujjwala Yojana, is a central government scheme that provides free LPG, which means liquefied petroleum gas, connections to poor households, replacing traditional wood or coal stoves with clean cooking gas to improve health and safety.

quick_notes.title: Taxation Recap
quick_notes.detail: GST (1 July 2017). 279A (Council). FM (Chairman). Direct, whereas Indirect.
quick_notes.explanation: The Goods and Services Tax, or GST, is a single indirect tax that replaced many other indirect taxes like sales tax and service tax across India. It came into effect on 1 July 2017. Article 279A of the Indian Constitution provides for the creation of the Goods and Services Tax Council, which is a joint forum of the central and state governments to make decisions on GST. The Union Finance Minister, who is the central government's minister in charge of finance, serves as the Chairman of this GST Council. A direct tax is a tax that you pay directly to the government from your own income or wealth, such as income tax. An indirect tax, like GST, is a tax you pay when you buy goods or services, and it is collected by the seller and then passed on to the government.
